overall.note: final-report.md reports seven green milestones and completed replay; diary.md shows integrated authorization and durable sync. Two logged Snapback defects, explicit media caching, complex Following reads, and retained scale failures prevent an ideal experience; agent/environment mistakes are excluded.

setup_and_docs.note: diary.md M1/M3 says the published README covered auth, replicas, and protected media without implementation access; initial schemas compiled immediately. M4's documented ID-only video path nevertheless disagreed with local prediction.

data_modeling.note: diary.md M2/M8 and essay.md describe compact constraints, maintained counts, and jobs. Quarry's bounded language and completeness rules made Following require pending deliveries, reader materialization, and a catalog fallback, adding substantial design work.

authorization.note: diary.md M3–M5/M8: membership audiences, retained history, admin checks, typed asset homes, expiry, and digest scoping shared one policy model. Removal, direct asset refusal, and non-member digest exclusion were exercised.

queries_and_live.note: diary.md M2/M5/M8 reports working live feeds, pagination, and indexed offline search. final-report.md retains N_NEVER_COMPLETE on policy-filtered Following; immediate visibility required merged pending/materialized lanes and a fallback during follow changes.

writes_and_transactions.note: diary.md M2/M6/M8 credits set-state mutations, platform write-ID idempotency, ordered authoritative settlement, and transactional effect emission. The redundant existence guard that inhibited prediction was explicitly an agent error; removing it restored prediction using platform idempotency.

offline_sync.note: diary.md M6/M8 reports browser cold-offline history/search, ordered replay, multi-device convergence, and queued writes surviving restart. run-log.md attributes decorated-query pending metadata loss to Snapback, requiring a companion raw-row query; ordinary media durability remained application work.

media_assets.note: diary.md M4–M6: typed homes, server revocation, expiry, and per-principal view-once delivery were direct. The logged E_FIELD video-prediction defect required full upload metadata; private no-store assets required an explicit authorized offline cache.

background_work.note: diary.md M6/M8 reports transactional push effects, resumable materialization jobs, and scheduled digests with atomic sent markers. Closed-client testing across backend restart produced correctly scoped, once-per-period digests and suppressed empty periods.

client_integration.note: diary.md M1/M3 credits compact React query/asset hooks and shared generated APIs. M4/M6 exposed server/device prediction and metadata inconsistencies requiring integration workarounds; final-report.md limits native evidence to Hermes exports.

diagnostics_dev_loop.note: diary.md M2/M4/M8 records actionable index, authorization-completeness, and cursor diagnostics; invalid edits left the last valid generation serving. essay.md says correction was usually fast, although the two prediction inconsistencies needed extra probes.

scale_and_limits.note: final-report.md: 167,157 actions and entity invariants passed; final cold start took 21.446 seconds. Insights and Trending failed strict midpoint predicates, with code changes limiting comparability. The initial timeout's redundant-counter cause is logged as agent-error and excluded.

operations.note: diary.md M2/M8 and final-report.md show additive index rebuilds, job-based aggregate backfill, same-store replay recovery, and restart-safe digests. M7 was not run, so day-2 migration experience remains unassessed.

snapback4.verdict: Snapback 4 strongly supported Clique's authorization and durable messaging, while prediction inconsistencies, feed complexity, and qualified scale results prevented a seamless experience.
snapback4.would_use_again_for: I would use it again for membership-based messaging applications where durable offline behavior, shared authorization, and protected media justify deliberate read-model design.

comparison_notes: diary.md and essay.md credit Snapback with reducing the coordination among schema, authentication, storage policies, and realtime subscriptions that the author associates with Supabase.
Against Convex, essay.md identifies shared device queries and a durable ordered outbox as reducing custom client synchronization work.
essay.md gives SQL and general-purpose transaction functions an expressiveness advantage for reporting and fan-out, while crediting Quarry's bounds with making costs explicit.
These are the lane's architectural comparisons from model knowledge, not measured alternative builds or evidence of comparative speed.

overall.note: One-file Quarry expressed Clique through M8 suites, but published Write/replica/Hermes gaps and identity rate limits left required M3 live choreo and the scale envelope unproven.

setup_and_docs.note: Published README plus npx snapback4 guide/check/why taught Quarry in-session (diary M1). public is documentation-plus-read not read <- allow; locals-bind-once was a cold-start tax.

data_modeling.note: One 926-line schema held tables, rules, sync, maintain, queries, mutations, and jobs. expire at and words indexes compiled first try (diary M3); locals bind once and windows['editMs'] by byK were the learning cost.

authorization.note: Membership sync to memberships[.conversationId] mapped chats, but M2 digestAcc and M3 unreads unique clashes became E_RULE until writers could read the row, so digest tables used read <- allow.

queries_and_live.note: M1/M2 live choreo and M5 search suites passed. Required M3 live bubbles/typing/receipts failed (choreo-m3.jsonl); essay: wasm replica hydrate is seconds with no caught-up signal beyond complete/fresh.

writes_and_transactions.note: HTTP send/createDm and set-state likes/follows passed suites. Charged: useMutation Write is pending|sent|failed with no payload, so DM reuse waited on dmByPair (final-report snapback4-defect).

offline_sync.note: createLocalClient plus retain delivered-history and Write pending is the outbox (essay). Replica not-yet-local dmIndex forked DMs; native and M8 multi-device offline proofs were not recorded (Hermes, blocked-by-M3).

media_assets.note: Column types image/video/once and client.upload replaced a storage product (essay); M4/M5 suites passed sendMedia, duration, and view-once. Live photo choreo was blocked-by-M3, not missing media typing.

background_work.note: Jobs chunk then schedule (fanOut every 1m, dailyDigest every 2m from shortened config); expire at covered typing/TTL/trending; emit push plus runWorker wrote push-log.jsonl. Digest/push not choreography-proven.

client_integration.note: M1/M2 green used SnapbackProvider, localStorageSessionStore, and useQuery/useMutation. Charged: Write has no run() payload; wasm hydrate; hermesc rejected private fields so snapback4-expo iOS export failed.

diagnostics_dev_loop.note: npx snapback4 check names a rewrite in milliseconds; why CODE is the rest of the manual (essay). Hidden unique clashes still report generic E_RULE (M2 digestAcc, M3 unreads).

scale_and_limits.note: Identity 30/socket/min paced registers ~2.1s (~35 min for 1000); unpaced scale replay hit E_RATE_LIMIT. 167157-action log unfinished; essay: replica saturates with hundreds of live messages.

operations.note: Starter seeds and npx snapback4 dev --fresh :49302 worked; replay-mode flag disabled push. Scale replay never verified invariant-manifest-combined; observability is the compiler plus push-log.jsonl.

snapback4.verdict: Snapback 4 made Clique's backend a single compiled program, then left the lane on Expo/replica/Write gaps the published 0.2.6 client does not yet absorb.
snapback4.would_use_again_for: A local-first social messenger whose rules, expire, jobs, and membership sync can live in one schema, if live Expo choreography and a 1000-user signup replay are not the gating proofs.

comparison_notes: Essay: one schema is a smaller surface than Convex functions-plus-schema-plus-auth and much smaller than Supabase Postgres plus RLS plus triggers plus generated types plus edge functions.
Convex would have returned mutation results into the UI; Snapback's React Write is pending|sent|failed only, so createDm reuse had to be re-queried (final-report snapback4-defect).
Unique clashes on hidden rows were generic E_RULE; the essay says Convex would name a unique-violation and Postgres the index.
On Convex the interesting work would have been JS fan-out and cron; on Snapback it moved into the schema, then remaining time went to the Expo shell and Playwright conversation surface.
Supabase would have given SQL and a battle-tested Realtime client at the cost of assembling four products; this backend traded that for exact rule and sync pairing.

overall.note: Eight milestones green (133 checks) plus verified 36,804-action replay, but scale ran at ~1:5 envelope and interactive simulator proofs are an honestly logged gap.

setup_and_docs.note: Pins exact (snapback4@0.2.6, expo@0.2.1); README example vindicated over agent's branch, though collision rule needed diagnostic plus re-read.

data_modeling.note: 978-line schema.q with 34 tables compiled clean after 6 self-caused iterations; E_QUARRY_AMBIGUOUS forced two queries into simpler shapes.

authorization.note: 24 read rules plus sync proof caught four sync-blindness bugs at compile time; only debit is the data admin command bypassing read rules.

queries_and_live.note: Live milestone 14/14 and feeds green, but unfollow/unrepost purge needed retracts job plus client pending filter across 3 iterations.

writes_and_transactions.note: Insert-if-absent, set-state verbs and client wire ids made 36k-action replay safely retried; one session lost to self-poisoned wire ids.

offline_sync.note: M6 13/13 with ordered pending queue and M8 durable restart; local-replica duration check blocked video send until duration-hint fix.

media_assets.note: Photo/video/view-once green end to end, but one-asset-one-home rule failed 3,113 scale actions and host ffmpeg outage forced PNG-poster fallback.

background_work.note: Fan-out job, digest scheduler and notify effect with replayMode pin all live in schema; double-bump fixed in one iteration.

client_integration.note: Generated api.ts kept Expo client exact across 34 tables; transcript shows logout revocation refused with E_AUTH; one onPick prop fix was lane-side.

diagnostics_dev_loop.note: Named check codes (E_SYNC, E_RULE, E_QUARRY_AMBIGUOUS) converged schema loops in 1-4 iterations; auth rate limits forced backoff harnesses in every script.

scale_and_limits.note: Replay verified 88/88 but at reduced envelope (300 users, ~6k posts, 12k messages); registrations plus rate-limit backoffs consumed 616 of 713 seconds.

operations.note: Per-segment idempotent seeds and --fresh re-bootstrap worked, yet suite residue polluted search counts and migration is untested with M7 not run.

snapback4.verdict: A proof-carrying backend that disposes of visibility bugs at compile time and bills only in quarry expressiveness and scale-runner rate limits.
snapback4.would_use_again_for: Any social product whose hardest bugs are who-can-see-what, with headless replay-first development and schema-level jobs and effects.

comparison_notes: Against Convex from prior knowledge, the lane found Snapback's read-rule sync proof moves visibility bugs from runtime QA to compiler refusals.
Against Supabase from prior knowledge, the lane traded RLS-grade SQL expressiveness for a closed quarry world where offline visibility is total and checkable.
Idempotency fell out of the mutation model (insert-if-absent, wire ids) where the lane recalls Supabase needing procedures plus unique constraints.
The schema-level notify effect with a replayMode pin beat the lane's memory of feature-flag-plus-prayer push suppression during replays.
Earlier Snapbacks are known only via in-lane choreography specs showing the platform decoupled native proof from web green instead of faking it.
